title: Research-Grounded Question Toolkit for AID Cycle
summary: Six research-grounded question forms (belief-mapping, pre-mortem, warrant elicitation, rebuttal elicitation, commitment gating, open-question reframing) the AID cycle composes with phase content; the non-formulaic requirement is a first-order constraint. Since ADR-100 the first pass of each form at a gate is performed by the agent on itself and the practitioner rules on the surviving pivot.

supersession.text: The six question forms and the phase-specific mapping stand. What changes: the first pass of each form at a gate is performed by the agent on itself (both sides developed, recommendation stated), and the practitioner's epistemic act is the ruling on the surviving pivot point.

links.note: first pass of each question form moves to the agent; forms and phase mapping unchanged; commitment gating becomes agent-proposed, practitioner-confirmed
